title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Chip swell lifts the Nasdaq as the Fed paddles out
conditions.summary: Chip stocks and AI names drove the Nasdaq up 1.2% and the S&P 500 up 0.6%, while the Dow was flat. Strong consumer confidence and lower oil helped ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: S&P 500 rose 0.60% to 7,722.60; Nasdaq gained 1.18% to 26,477.81.
Dow edged up 0.03% to 52,377.57; Russell 2000 rose 1.16% to 2,818.87.
Chips led: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped about 3.6%, with all 30 members higher.
AI enthusiasm got a lift from Anthropic's IPO filing, and falling oil helped sentiment.
Technology and materials led sectors; energy, consumer staples and real estate lagged.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: Conference Board consumer confidence rose to 91.7 in October, well above the roughly 81 expected.
September new home sales came in at a 676,000 annual pace, down 0.6% from August.
The Fed began its two-day meeting; markets price about 90% odds of a hold at 3.75% to 4%, with focus on a possible December hike.
The 10-year yield held near 4.99%, about unchanged; the dollar index firmed above 102.
WTI crude fell about 1.7% to near $100; gold rose about 0.9% to about $4,074; bitcoin was near $80,500; the VIX fell to about 17.5.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: PNR (Pentair): +11.8% — beat third-quarter estimates and signaled a turnaround.
SOFI (SoFi Technologies): +11.3% — earnings beat and upbeat long-term growth outlook.
BE (Bloom Energy): +7.8% — beat and raised its 2026 revenue forecast.
CRWV (CoreWeave): +7.9% — AI cloud stocks rebounded with the chip rally.
BA (Boeing): about -10% — missed estimates and cut its full-year delivery target.
XYL (Xylem): about -8.9% — missed estimates and cut full-year guidance.
CTAS (Cintas): -7.1% — reports the FTC plans to block its $5.5 billion UniFirst deal.
VLO (Valero): -6.6% — refiners slid as crude prices pulled back.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Before the open: Coca-Cola beat on earnings and revenue but slipped 1.6% on flat North American volume.
Before the open: UPS beat and raised its full-year revenue outlook to about $92.6 billion; Royal Caribbean beat and raised guidance.
After the close: Visa beat on EPS ($3.48 vs $3.44) but slipped about 2% after hours; Robinhood fell about 5% on a revenue miss.
After the close: Seagate beat but fell about 7%; Enphase missed and dropped about 10%; PPG beat and rose about 7.5%.

sections.title: Business News
items: Anthropic filed for an IPO on the Nasdaq, reporting $16.29 billion in revenue for the six months ended June.
Anthropic agreed to pay SpaceX up to $120.5 billion for computing infrastructure through 2029.
Meta upsized its common stock offering to $25 billion at $625 a share; Nvidia plans to invest $3 billion in Meta.
General Motors said it will move its listing from the NYSE to Nasdaq.
The US government offered Constellation Energy up to $5 billion in conditional financing for nuclear upgrades.

sections.title: On Deck
items: ADP employment report before the open.
Fed rate decision at 1:00 PM CT; Chair Warsh press conference at 1:30 PM CT.
Before the open: GE Vernova and Phillips 66 report earnings.
After the close: Microsoft, Alphabet and Chipotle report.
Thursday: September PCE inflation; Amazon, Intel and Coinbase report after the close.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Tuesday, October twenty-seventh, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sinking into the Gulf, and I'm waxing the board for tomorrow. Gus the wonder dog chased sandpipers down by the pier all afternoon. Say good evening, Gus! Here's the final set. The S and P 500 rose six tenths of a percent to about seven thousand seven hundred twenty-three. The Nasdaq hung ten, up one point two percent to about twenty-six thousand four hundred seventy-eight. The Dow was flat near fifty-two thousand three hundred seventy-eight. The Russell 2000 gained one point two percent. Chips made the big swell. The semiconductor index jumped about three and a half percent. AI buzz helped after Anthropic filed to go public. Tech led, while energy and staples lagged. Wind and weather. Consumer confidence rose to ninety-one point seven, far above the roughly eighty-one expected. New home sales dipped slightly. The Fed began its two-day meeting, and markets see about a ninety percent chance of a hold. The ten-year yield sat near four point nine nine percent, barely changed. The dollar firmed above one hundred two. Crude slid about one point seven percent to near one hundred dollars. Gold rose almost one percent. Bitcoin was near eighty thousand five hundred, and the VIX fell to about seventeen and a half. The lineup. Pentair surged almost twelve percent on a strong quarter. SoFi Technologies rode a beat and an upbeat outlook to an eleven percent gain. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! Bloom Energy and CoreWeave each rose almost eight percent. Boeing took a gnarly wipeout, down about ten percent after a miss and a delivery target cut. Xylem fell about nine percent, Cintas about seven on merger trouble, and Valero six and a half as oil eased. Tide chart. Coca-Cola beat but slipped about one and a half percent. UPS beat and raised its outlook. After the bell, Visa beat but dipped about two percent. Robinhood fell about five percent and Seagate about seven. P P G jumped about seven and a half percent. Beach talk. Anthropic, the newest grom paddling toward the public lineup, reported more than sixteen billion dollars in first half revenue. Meta upsized its stock offering to twenty-five billion dollars. General Motors will move its listing to the Nasdaq. Tomorrow's forecast. The A D P jobs report comes before the open. The Fed decision hits at one P M Central, with Chair Warsh at one thirty. Microsoft and Alphabet report after the close. Want a read on any stock, E T F or futures contract? Type it into the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. Soul surfers ride every tide. Catch Dawn Patrol tomorrow morning. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
